:::{#thm-biconditional-split}
#### A biconditional is two conditionals

For [propositions](#def-proposition) $P$ and $Q$,

$$
(P \Leftrightarrow Q) \equiv \paren{(P \Rightarrow Q) \land (Q \Rightarrow P)}.
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

By the definitions of [if and only if](#def-iff), [implies](#def-implies) and [and](#def-and),
the [truth table](#def-truth-table) is:

| $P$ | $Q$ | $P \Rightarrow Q$ | $Q \Rightarrow P$ | $(P \Rightarrow Q) \land (Q \Rightarrow P)$ | $P \Leftrightarrow Q$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| T | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | F | F | T | F | F |
| F | T | T | F | F | F |
| F | F | T | T | T | T |

The last two columns match in every row,
so the two [propositions](#def-proposition) are [logically equivalent](#def-logically-equivalent).

:::

:::
